'''Maria Wetterstrand''' (born 2 October 1973) is a Swedish politician. She was one of the spokespersons of the [[Green Party (Sweden)|Green Party]] alongside [[Peter Eriksson (Swedish Green Party politician)|Peter Eriksson]] between 2002 and 2011. Between 2001 and 2011 she was a [[List of members of the Swedish Riksdag|member]] of the [[Parliament of Sweden|Riksdag]].

She was born on 2 October 1973 in [[Eskilstuna]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Billing |first=Sören |date=2023-06-21 |title=”När jag var politiker hade jag väldigt mycket fördomar om näringslivet” |url=https://www.sydsvenskan.se/artikel/nar-jag-var-politiker-hade-jag-valdigt-mycket-fordomar-om-naringslivet/ |access-date=2025-08-23 |work=[[Sydsvenskan]] |language=sv}}</ref>

Wetterstrand has a master's degree in biology from the [[University of Gothenburg]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010-08-23 |title=Maria Wetterstrand |url=https://www.svt.se/nyheter/inrikes/maria-wetterstrand |access-date=2025-08-23 |work=SVT Nyheter |language=sv}}</ref>

Wetterstrand was married to [[Ville Niinistö]], a Finnish politician representing the [[Green League]], between 2004 and 2012. They have two children: a son born in October 2004 and a daughter born 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/article10469036.ab |title=Grattis... Maria Wetterstrand |publisher=Aftonbladet.se |date=5 July 2004 |accessdate=27 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/article14944753.ab |title=Nu går paret skilda vägar &#124; Nyheter &#124; Aftonbladet |publisher=Aftonbladet.se |date=7 June 2012 |accessdate=28 September 2012}}</ref>
